item.title: Opinion: Winning the War, Testing the Constitution
item.description: The campaign against Iran’s nuclear infrastructure may come to be remembered as one of the most consequential strategic operations in decades. In coordination with Israel, the United States helped deliver a stunning blow to a regime that spent years racing toward nuclear capability while threatening Israel’s destruction and destabilizing the Middle East.

item.title: Why There’s Always Wasabi at My Seder
item.description: Shank bone, check. Haroset, check. Everything is there, on smooth pottery, but wait — is that … wasabi? This is the one item on my seder plate that draws smiles, and I get it. It’s not the norm. It’s my take on a bitter herb, maror. Welcome to our Passover in Japan!

item.title: D'var Torah: Making Meaningful Sacrifices
item.description: This week’s Torah portion is Vayikra. In this portion, God, through Moses, instructs the Israelites on how to do their required sacrifices. These sacrifices were how the Israelites connected with God and were the base of their religious life. There were four main kinds of sacrifices. The olah, the burnt offering, was brought to thank God and express gratitude. It was also brought as part of the daily and festival services.

item.title: Letter to the Editor: ‘A Sneer at Shabbat’ (Editorial, March 13)
item.description: Gregory Bovino’s reported sarcastic and demeaning remarks about Jews and the Sabbath are consistent with his outrageous behavior as a commander-at-large and senior enforcement official within the U.S. Customs and Border Patrol Agency.

item.title: Opinion: As a Genocide Law Professor, I’d Give the US Brief Supporting Israel at the ICJ a Failing Grade
item.description: A detailed legal analysis of the United States' intervention in the International Court of Justice case, South Africa v. Israel.

item.title: Opinion: At Temple Israel, Both Security Training and Sacred Relationships Prepared Us for the Worst
item.description: Security preparation can alter your instincts and equip you to respond effectively in critical situations.

item.title: Israel Fully Reopens Gaza’s Rafah Crossing With Egypt
item.description: The Rafah Crossing between southern Gaza and Egypt has been reopened in both directions.

item.title: In Settlement, UC Berkeley Agrees Bans on Zionists ‘Can Violate University Rules’
item.description: UC Berkeley said bans on Zionists “can violate university rules” and the bylaws of any student groups barring their inclusion must be rescinded.

item.title: Opinion: Finding Meaning in the Mundane: Connecting With the Source That Fuels Us
item.description: Last week, six American servicemembers tragically lost their lives during a mid-air refueling mission over Iraq connected to the current war with Iran. The details were sparse, but the incident highlighted one of the most complex and delicate maneuvers in modern aviation.

item.title: Maryland Man Sentenced to Prison for Threatening Jewish Institutions
item.description: A Maryland man was sentenced to more than three years in federal prison after pleading guilty to mailing threatening letters to Jewish institutions, according to a March 16 press release.
